thread.title: Apple Earnings: What To Look For In Its Fiscal Third-Quarter Report

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Apple Earnings: What To Look For In Its Fiscal Third-Quarter Report
text:
Consumer electronics giant Apple ( AAPL ) is scheduled to report its June-quarter results after the market close on Tuesday. But investors will tune in more for the company's predictions for the current quarter when its next-generation iPhones are due.
X Several Wall Street analysts on Monday revealed what they'll be looking for from the latest Apple earnings report. On average, analysts expect Apple to earn $2.18 a share on sales of $52.34 billion for the period, its fiscal third quarter . That would translate to year-over-year growth of 31% in earnings per share and 15% in sales.
In addition to those top- and bottom-line numbers, investors will be paying close attention to iPhone unit sales, average selling price and revenue from services. They'll also be looking for clues to the company's expectations for its 12th-generation iPhones, due in September.
Wall Street expects Apple to report sales of 41.8 million iPhone units in the June quarter. That compares with 41 million units in the year-earlier period. The analyst view for iPhone average selling price is $693, according to FactSet.

Please contact customer service CLOSE Apple Sells More Higher-Priced iPhones "Apple is having success moving buyers up the iPhone price curve," UBS analyst Timothy Arcuri said in a report Monday. He noted that 26% of customers paid more than $900 for an iPhone in the March quarter, compared with just 5% a year earlier.
He expects iPhone average selling prices to rise again in the September quarter, thanks to the latest iPhones.
Arcuri reiterated his buy rating on Apple stock with a 12-month price target of 210. Apple dipped 0.6% to close at 189.91 on the stock market today .
Analysts are looking for iPhone revenue of $29.14 billion in the June quarter. FactSet dubs services as Apple's second largest revenue category, with $9.21 billion in expected sales.
Apple might be cautious with its orders for the next-generation iPhones, Arcuri said.
"While our supply chain work suggests rather pedestrian supply, to us this sets a low bar where the bias is to the upside," he said. He is modeling 80 million new iPhones built this calendar year vs. 95 million to 100 million initial orders for last year's iPhones.
Apple's Expanding Services Business Monness Crespi Hardt analyst Brian White said he doesn't expect any big surprises from Apple's third-quarter report. He maintained his buy rating on Apple stock with a price target of 235.
"We are not expecting any fireworks during this earnings report given the uncertainty inherent with any new iPhone launch that is usually reflected in Apple's September-quarter guidance, combined with an onerous foreign exchange headwind," he said in a report. "However, we believe Apple's strong software capabilities, expanding services business and unique digital ecosystem at large are increasingly being appreciated by the market."
For the September quarter, Wall Street is modeling Apple to earn $2.65 a share on sales of $59.57 billion. That would translate to growth of 28% in earnings per share and 13% in sales.
Apple Feeling 'Fortnite' Effect RBC Capital Markets analyst Amit Daryanani expects Apple to post "strong services momentum" in the June quarter.
Services growth will be led by subscriptions, such as Apple Music, and mobile gaming, including the hugely popular "Fortnite Battle Royale" from Epic Games, he said.
He kept his outperform rating on Apple stock and his price target of 210.
